verdicts.question: What type of roof is present at the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 7-8 (Staircase Details, Material Storage) and p11 (Proposed PV Area) show a flat concrete terrace with plastered parapet walls, concrete headroom and red-oxide RCC steps; no tiles or metal sheeting on the main roof (only a small red sheet pergola).
verdicts.rationale: Flat RCC terrace is clearly visible in multiple rooftop photos; matches designer answer.

verdicts.question: Are there any obstructions on the roof that could affect the solar installation?
verdicts.designer_answer: details: Solar water heater will affect the solar installation.
verdicts.photo_observation: p7 and p11 show a 'Supreme Solar' evacuated-tube solar water heater sitting in the proposed PV area; p11 caption says it will be removed by the customer. Also visible: yellow water tank on top of the headroom, metal ladder, wooden board, red sheet pergola.
verdicts.rationale: SWH obstruction is clearly present as stated. Note that its removal is a customer-scope dependency, and the water tank/headroom/ladder are additional obstructions not mentioned (the elevated design appears to clear them).

verdicts.question: What is the angle of the panels? (in degrees)
verdicts.photo_observation: No real-photo of the installed tilt (proposed system). 3D model on p9 (side views) and p10 ('Structure front clearance 2.0m') shows a shallow single-direction tilt that looks roughly 8-12 deg.
verdicts.rationale: Design renders are consistent with a ~10 deg tilt; cannot be measured precisely from images.

verdicts.question: On how many roofs at the site are we installing solar?
verdicts.photo_observation: p8 top view and p9 side views show a single 6-module array (2 rows x 3) on one terrace; p11 marks a single 'PV propose area'.
verdicts.rationale: One contiguous array on one roof, matching '1'.

verdicts.question: What type of mounting structure is planned?
verdicts.photo_observation: p9 side views and p10 'Structure front clearance' render show the array on tall steel columns with 2.0 m front clearance above the terrace.
verdicts.rationale: Elevated structure is clearly shown in the design renders.

verdicts.question: What is the orientation of the solar panels?
verdicts.photo_observation: p8 top view has a north arrow pointing up. In p9 side view (1) the compass 'N' points left and the array's low edge is on the right, i.e. the panels face away from north (south).
verdicts.rationale: Compass cues in the 3D model are consistent with south-facing panels; no GMap overlay to confirm the real building orientation.

verdicts.question: How can the roof be accessed?
verdicts.photo_observation: p6 top photo shows an internal granite staircase with railing; p7 'Staircase Details' and p8 'Material Storage' show RCC steps leading onto the terrace through the headroom.
verdicts.rationale: Fixed staircase access to the roof is clearly visible.

verdicts.question: Is the building currently under construction?
verdicts.photo_observation: p5 'Building Exterior' and p6 show a finished, painted/plastered house with fitted windows, gate, jali balconies, parked car and occupants; no scaffolding or bare brickwork.
verdicts.rationale: Building is clearly completed and occupied.

verdicts.question: What is the height of the building and how many floors does it have?
verdicts.designer_answer: Height of the building is 14m; it has G+3 floors
verdicts.photo_observation: p6 bottom photo (side elevation) shows windows at ground level (above compound wall), a round-window level, one more window level, then the terrace with a red-sheet pergola - reads as G+2 + terrace headroom. p5 front shows ground floor window and two jali balconies, with a possible further parapet level hidden by sun flare.
verdicts.rationale: Visible floor count appears to be G+2 + headroom rather than G+3; sun flare and wide-angle distortion prevent a firm count. Verify floors/14m height (and whether a basement exists, as earth pits are described as 'basement area').

verdicts.question: Is the site photo matching with the building description?
verdicts.photo_observation: Exterior photos (p5, p6, p13) show a residential RCC building with flat terrace and headroom, consistent with the description, but the visible floor count looks like G+2 + headroom vs stated G+3.
verdicts.rationale: General description matches; floor-count discrepancy (see roof_13) needs confirmation before accepting 'Yes'.

verdicts.question: Is there an overhead HT line passing within a 10-meter radius of the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: p5 shows a bundle of 4-5 overhead conductors running diagonally past the front facade at 1st-2nd floor level, within ~1-3 m of the balconies; p6/p13 show more overhead wires crossing near the top corner of the building and a roadside pole.
verdicts.rationale: Overhead lines are clearly within 10 m of the building. They look like LT distribution conductors rather than an 11 kV HT line (no tall HT pole/insulator strings visible), but voltage class cannot be confirmed from photos - verify on site.

verdicts.question: Can the delivery van/truck reach the material unloading point?
verdicts.photo_observation: p5 'Material Delivery Route' shows a car parked directly at the front gate on a paved/earth approach; p6 shows an unpaved road alongside the building.
verdicts.rationale: Vehicle access up to the gate is clearly visible.

verdicts.question: Are there any obstacles at the site that could hinder material lifting?
verdicts.photo_observation: p6 bottom photo marks the large-item (panel) hoisting route up the side wall (cyan line). A tree grows right beside the wall with foliage overlapping the route up to ~2nd floor, overhead wires cross near the top corner of the building, and the ground at the base is dense overgrown shrubs. Front facade (p5) also has overhead conductors close to the balconies.
verdicts.rationale: Photos show potential lifting obstacles (tree canopy along hoist line, nearby overhead wires, overgrown base) that contradict an unqualified 'No'; needs reviewer confirmation of whether these impede rope lifting.

verdicts.question: Where will the Inverter, DCDB, ACDB, Battery, etc. be located?
verdicts.designer_answer: Inverter, DCDB, ACDB, Battery is located near the top terrace.
verdicts.photo_observation: p12 top photo shows a covered concrete alcove on the terrace (next to the SWH) annotated 'Inverter and other components', 'Battery' and 'UPS point'; an existing battery/UPS currently occupies it (caption: to be removed by customer).
verdicts.rationale: Equipment location on the terrace is clearly shown and annotated.

verdicts.question: Is a canopy required for protecting the Inverters/ACDB/DCDB?
verdicts.photo_observation: p12 top photo: the equipment alcove has an RCC slab overhead and plastered walls on three sides, open only at the front.
verdicts.rationale: Location is sheltered by the existing slab; no extra canopy appears necessary. Front opening faces the terrace, so some rain splash is possible.

verdicts.question: Did you discuss the location of the earth pits with the customer?
verdicts.designer_answer: Location of the earth pits are in the basement area.
verdicts.photo_observation: p13 'Earth Pit Location' bottom photo shows LA, DC and AC earth pits marked in a narrow ground-level side passage between the building wall and the compound wall; the floor is concrete-paved. p13 top shows earthing/LA runs (green/orange) down the side facade.
verdicts.rationale: Earth pit location is documented, but the photo shows a ground-level paved side setback, not a basement - wording mismatch and paved surface (needs breaking) should be confirmed.

verdicts.question: Where is the Internet Router located?
verdicts.photo_observation: No photo of a router or network point in the photo pages. p14 Observations lists 'Wi-Fi is under customer scope'.
verdicts.rationale: Not visually verifiable; the text observation is consistent, but no router location is documented.

verdicts.question: Did you pin the site location in your WhatsApp when you were at the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Not a visual item. Page 1 contains GPS coordinates 13.0780, 77.7073 and a Google Maps link.
verdicts.rationale: WhatsApp pin cannot be verified from photos; GPS coordinates in the report are supportive only.

verdicts.question: What type of energy meter is currently installed?
verdicts.designer_answer: Phase: Three Phase, Type: Digital, If 3-phase: LT w/o CT (5 - 34.999)
verdicts.photo_observation: p7 'Meter Box': Landis+Gyr E250 meter labelled '3-PHASE 4 WIRE ENERGY METER' with LCD display; red/yellow/blue phase cables wired directly into the meter terminals (no CTs) and three fuse cut-outs below.
verdicts.rationale: Digital, whole-current three-phase meter with no CTs is clearly visible.

verdicts.question: Is the Meter cubicle photo matching with the previous answer?
verdicts.photo_observation: p7 meter cubicle photo shows the 3-phase digital direct-connected meter with three phase cut-outs; p12 shows the same cubicle in the main panel assembly.
verdicts.rationale: Cubicle photo matches the stated three-phase digital LT meter.

verdicts.question: Has the termination point in the Main meter panel been identified?
verdicts.photo_observation: p12 'Equipment Location' marks the 'Main meter' cubicle and a purple AC line from the proposed 'Solar meter' into it; p7 shows the three outgoing fuse cut-outs inside.
verdicts.rationale: Termination at the main meter panel is annotated; exact terminal point not individually labelled.

verdicts.question: Is the Termination Point easily visible or sealed?
verdicts.photo_observation: p7: meter terminals are visible through a transparent terminal cover, but the cover carries a blue utility seal on the right side; the fuse cut-outs below are exposed and accessible.
verdicts.rationale: Cut-outs are visible, but the meter terminal cover is sealed - confirm which point is intended as the termination.

verdicts.question: Is a Lightning Arrestor (LA) already available at the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: No lightning arrestor rod is visible in any rooftop photo (p7, p8, p11, p12); the LA in the 3D model (p8-p9) is a proposed new item.
verdicts.rationale: Absence of LA in rooftop photos is consistent with 'No'.

verdicts.question: In Main meter panel, is empty space available for solar meter?
verdicts.photo_observation: p7: meter cubicle is fully occupied by the main meter and three cut-outs. p12: adjacent compartments hold a second enclosure with analog meters; the solar meter is proposed outside, on the wall to the left of the panel.
verdicts.rationale: No spare space in the main meter cubicle is visible; solar meter is planned outside.

verdicts.question: Is there space available to dig DC, AC and LA earth pits?
verdicts.photo_observation: p13 bottom photo shows a long side passage (~1 m wide) with three pit positions (LA, DC, AC) marked along it; surface is concrete-paved.
verdicts.rationale: Space for three pits is shown, though the paved surface will need to be broken.

verdicts.question: What type of Earthing chamber needs to be installed at site? Is it Cement chamber or PVC chamber?
verdicts.photo_observation: p13 shows the proposed pit positions in a paved passage; no chamber type visible (new installation).
verdicts.rationale: Chamber type is a design choice not verifiable from photos.

verdicts.question: In case of elevated structures, is an LA extension provided at the far end?
verdicts.photo_observation: p8 top view and p9 side views show a yellow 'LA' marker mounted at the corner of the elevated array (near the headroom/SWH).
verdicts.rationale: LA is shown at the array edge in the design renders; whether this is the 'far end' is a design interpretation.

verdicts.question: In case of elevated structures, is it with or without grouting?
verdicts.photo_observation: No photo or render detail of column base plates/foundations; p10 render shows plain base plates only.
verdicts.rationale: Grouting cannot be verified from images.

verdicts.question: Are there any challenges with respect to Installation and Maintenance activities?
verdicts.photo_observation: Photos show: SWH in the PV area that must be removed (p11), existing battery/UPS occupying the equipment alcove that must be removed (p12), 2.0 m elevated structure over a terrace with headroom/ladder/water tank (p9-p11), and overhead wires/tree near the hoisting route (p6).
verdicts.rationale: Several customer-scope dependencies and work-at-height factors are visible; 'No' challenges should be confirmed.

verdicts.question: Are there any safety risks associated with accessing the roof for installation?
verdicts.photo_observation: p6 internal staircase with railing and p7/p8 RCC steps onto a terrace with parapet walls - fixed, railed access.
verdicts.rationale: Roof access route looks safe; working-at-height on the 2 m elevated structure is a separate consideration.

verdicts.question: Is space present in rooftop to store the panels?
verdicts.photo_observation: p8 'Material Storage' shows an open terrace area beside the headroom steps with plain plastered walls/parapet suitable for leaning panels.
verdicts.rationale: Clear wall space for vertical panel storage is visible.

verdicts.question: Is ventilation available in the battery location?
verdicts.photo_observation: p12 top: battery location is a terrace alcove open fully on the front side to the outside air.
verdicts.rationale: Open-fronted alcove provides natural ventilation.

verdicts.question: Is Battery wall mounted or stand mounted?
verdicts.photo_observation: p12 top: alcove has plastered walls; the existing (to-be-removed) battery sits on the floor. Proposed battery shown only as an annotation box on the wall.
verdicts.rationale: Proposed mounting method is not visible; wall surface appears suitable but cannot confirm.

verdicts.question: Should the Inverters/ACDB/DCDB be installed on a metal grill or wall mount?
verdicts.designer_answer: Inverters/ACDB/D CDB be installed on a wall mount
verdicts.photo_observation: p12 top: 'Inverter and other components' annotation is placed on the solid plastered back wall of the alcove; no metal grill present.
verdicts.rationale: Solid wall is available for wall mounting.

verdicts.question: Provide the dimensions for solar meter cubicle placement (L x W of wall).
verdicts.photo_observation: p12 'Equipment Location': solar meter proposed on the plain wall to the left of the main meter panel; free wall area visible but no measurement marked.
verdicts.rationale: Wall space appears available, but 800 x 400 cannot be verified from the photo (units also unstated).

verdicts.question: Provide the dimension for earth pits location (L x W of available space).
verdicts.photo_observation: p13 bottom: earth pits are in a narrow side passage roughly 1 m wide between the building and compound wall.
verdicts.rationale: Units unstated: if cm, a 250 cm width does not fit the ~1 m passage; if mm, it is too small for the space shown. Verify dimensions/units.

verdicts.question: Is LAN cable under customer scope?
verdicts.photo_observation: No network/LAN photo. p14 Observations state 'Wi-Fi is under customer scope' and general Q6 says router is 'customer scope'.
verdicts.rationale: Not visually verifiable; check consistency with Wi-Fi/router being customer scope.

verdicts.question: Is there any shadow that affects the solar installation?
verdicts.photo_observation: p11 rooftop view: surroundings are open with low neighbouring buildings and trees below roof level. Water tank sits on the headroom on the north side of the array (p8 top view); SWH in the array area is to be removed. Array is elevated 2 m.
verdicts.rationale: No significant shading objects to the south/east/west visible; depends on SWH removal by the customer.

verdicts.question: Is there any trench work to be done to carry the AC cable to the meter location?
verdicts.photo_observation: Meter panel (p12) is mounted on the building wall; routes are drawn down the exterior facade (p6/p13) with no open-ground crossing shown.
verdicts.rationale: Route appears to run on building walls only; no trench indicated.

verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run - from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel - with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?
verdicts.photo_observation: p11: 'Cable Routing' heading has no photo under it. p11 top/p12 top show red/green lines from the PV area along the parapet into the terrace alcove (inverter/battery). p12 bottom shows only a short purple AC line from the 'Solar meter' into the 'Main meter' at the ground-floor panel. The vertical AC run from the terrace inverter down to the ground-floor solar meter is not drawn anywhere; p13 facade lines are earthing/LA (green/orange) only. No conduit/clipping details shown.
verdicts.rationale: Documented route has a gap: inverter (terrace) -> solar meter (ground floor) AC run is missing, and the Cable Routing section is empty. Also note: 1-phase Deye 5 kW inverter specified with a 3-phase service - confirm phase connection.
